title: security.txt must be served as text/plain with charset utf-8

cites.quote: It MUST have a Content-Type of "text/plain" with the default charset parameter set to "utf-8" (as per Section 4.1.3 of [RFC2046]).
cites.note: Transcribed from a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-10-29 (file sha256 79d19ce7a4a35496981095a27fd992797a9fc4d6f3649c2a1e14f494607c61f9). Lines 450-452. The header comes from the serving platform (the Worker's static-asset plane), not from the file, so this rule judges the HTTP response, not the body.

policy_note: An absent charset parameter passes. The sentence names utf-8 as the DEFAULT charset, and sectxt (the reference checker, DigitalTrustCenter/sectxt) reads a missing parameter as utf-8 the same way. The IANA alias csUTF8 passes too, as it does in sectxt. Media type, parameter name and charset name compare case-insensitively (RFC 2045 §5.1, RFC 2046 §4.1.2), and a quoted charset value is unquoted first. A missing header fails: the sentence requires the header.
applicability: The Content-Type header of a 2xx response for SECURITY_TXT_URL. main() reads it with res.headers.get('content-type') and passes it to validateSecurityTxtContentType; a case input is a JSON object {"contentType": <string or null>}.
expectation: The header is present; its media type, trimmed and lowercased, is text/plain; every charset parameter, unquoted and lowercased, is utf-8 or csutf8.

cases.name: text/plain; charset=utf-8 -- the production header on 2026-10-29
text/plain with no charset -- utf-8 is the default
mixed case and a quoted charset still match
the IANA alias csUTF8 names UTF-8
